Usage: qsys-generate <file>

   OPTION                                               DESCRIPTION
   <1st arg file>                                       .qsys or .ip file
   -syn, --synthesis[=<VERILOG|VHDL|SYSTEM_VERILOG>]  ? Create synthesis files.
   -bsf, --block-symbol-file                          ? Create block symbol file (.bsf).
   -greybox, --greybox                                ? Create timing and resource estimates for third-parth EDA synthesis.
   -ipxact, --ipxact                                  ? Create an IPXACT representation of your system.
   -sim, --simulation[=<VERILOG|VHDL|SYSTEM_VERILOG>] ? Create simulation model.
   -tb, --testbench[=<SIMPLE|STANDARD>]               ? Create testbench system.
   -tb-sim, --testbench-simulation[=<VERILOG|VHDL|    ? Create simulation model for the testbench system.
   SYSTEM_VERILOG>]                                   
   -ed, --example-design[=<value>]                    ? Create example design files.
   -sp, --search-path=<value>                         ? IP component search path 
   --family=<value>                                   ? The device family
   --part=<value>                                     ? The device part
   --board[=<value>]                                  ? The board
   -qpf, --quartus-project=<value>                    ? Quartus project
   -c, --rev=<value>                                  ? Quartus project revision
   -uvf, --upgrade-variation-file                     ? Enables upgrading a megawizard variation file to a Platform Designer format file
   -uic, --upgrade-ip-cores                           ? Enables upgrading all the ip cores that are available in the Platform Designer system.
   -cod , --clear-output-directory                    ? Clears the output directory corresponding to the selected target, i.e. simulation or synthesis.
   -eqs, --export-qsys-script                         ? Exports the .qsys file system as a Platform Designer script file (.tcl).
   -oipv, --omit-ip-version                           ? Omit the requested IP version when exporting the .qsys file system as a Platform Designer script file (.tcl).
   -top, --top-level-generation                       ? Generate Top
   -doc, --documentation                              ? Emit core-defined documentation files.
   -b, --batch=<value>                                * Add file to batch generate.
   -gass, --generate-all-simulation-scripts           ? Generate simulation scripts for entire hierarchy
   -mf, --modelsim-flow[=<TRADITIONAL|QRUN>]          ? Specifies the Questasim flow used for simulation script generation.
   -par, --parallel[=<value>]                         ? If omitted, or no value specified, best attempt is made to use the available cores in the system for parallel generation. A value greater than 1 can be specified to indicate the level of parallelism to use. To disable parallel generation, set value to "off".
   -pemhs, --parallel-executors-max-heap-size=<value> ? Set the maximum heap memory size to be used by parallel execution modules in parallel mode.
   -bqp, --bypass-quartus-project                     ? Bypass quartus project
   -smltr, --simulator[=<value>]                      * Specifies the simulator type(s) for which simulation scripts will be generated.
   -svw, --system-verilog-wrapper                     ? Create a SystemVerilog top-level wrapper when generating Verilog synthesis or simulation generation targets.
   --jvm-max-heap-size=<value>                        ? Set the maximum heap memory size to be used
   -h, --help                                         ? Show help

QSYS-GENERATE
-------------
Generate HDL and other output files for system file(s) and/or ip
files(s).

<1st arg file>
     Required. The name of the .qsys system file to generate.

--synthesis[=<VERILOG|VHDL|SYSTEM_VERILOG>]
     Optional. Create synthesis HDL files, used to compile the system in
     a Quartus Prime project. The default is "VERILOG".

--block-symbol-file
     Optional. Create a block symbol file (.bsf) for the system.

--greybox
     Optional. If you are synthesizing your design with a third-party
     EDA synthesis tool, you can generate a netlist for the synthesis
     tool to estimate timing and resource usage for this design.

--ipxact
     Optional. When the value of this switch is true, the
     post-generation system will be rendered as an IPXACT-compatible
     component description.

--simulation[=<VERILOG|VHDL|SYSTEM_VERILOG>]
     Optional. Create a simulation model for the system. The simulation
     model contains generated HDL files for the simulator, and may
     include simulation-only features. The default is "VERILOG".

--testbench[=<SIMPLE|STANDARD>]
     Optional. Create a testbench system. The testbench system
     instantiates the original system, adding bus functional models to
     drive the top-level interfaces. Once generated, the bus functional
     models can interact with the system in the simulator. The default
     is "STANDARD".

--testbench-simulation[=<VERILOG|VHDL|SYSTEM_VERILOG>]
     Optional. After creating the testbench system, also create a
     simulation model for the testbench system. The default is
     "VERILOG".

--example-design[=<value>]
     Optional. Create example design files. For example:
     --example-design (or) --example-design=all. The default is "All",
     which generates example designs for all instances. Alternatively,
     you can choose specific filesets based on instance name and fileset
     name. For example
     --example-design=instance0.example_design1,instance1.example_design
     2. You can also specify an output directory to where the files will
     be created.

--search-path=<value>
     Optional. If omitted, a standard default path will be used. If
     provided, a comma-separated list of paths will be searched. To
     include the standard path in your replacement, use "$", like
     "/extra/dir,$".

--family=<value>
     Optional. Set the device family.

--part=<value>
     Optional. Set the device part number. If set, this option overrides
     the "--family" option.

--board[=<value>]
     Optional. Set the board.

--quartus-project=<value>
     Optional. The name of the Quartus project file. You may provide the
     revision name using --rev; otherwise, the default revision
     associated with the Quartus project is used.

--rev=<value>
     Optional. The name of the Quartus project revision. This switch is
     ignored if it is provided without one of the Quartus project
     switches.

--upgrade-variation-file
     Optional. When the value of this switch is true, the file argument
     for this command will accept a ".v" filewhich contains a megawizard
     variant. This file will parameterize a corresponding instance in a
     Platform Designer system of the same name.

--upgrade-ip-cores
     Optional. Enables upgrading all the ip cores that are available in
     the Platform Designer system.

--clear-output-directory
     Optional. Clears the output directory corresponding to the selected
     target, i.e. simulation or synthesis. 

--export-qsys-script
     Optional. When the value of this switch is true, the
     post-generation system will be exported as a Platform Designer
     script file with the extension (.tcl).

--omit-ip-version
     Optional. When the value of this switch is true, the generated
     Platform Designer script (.tcl) will not include the requested IP
     version. Use along with --export-qsys-script switch

--top-level-generation
     Optional. Only generate the top level of the given system, do not
     descend into hierarchy, do not generate Generic Components.

--documentation
     Optional. Emit the core-defined documentation (if any) for each of
     the IP instances in your system.

--batch=<value>
     Optional. Repeatable. Add the given system or stand-alone IP to the
     list of files to batch generate.

--generate-all-simulation-scripts
     Optional. Generate simulation scripts for the top-level system, as
     well as all subsystems and ip.

--modelsim-flow[=<TRADITIONAL|QRUN>]
     Optional. Specifies the Questasim flow (qrun or traditional) used
     for simulation script generation. If not specified, the qrun flow
     will be used.

--parallel[=<value>]
     Optional. If omitted, or no value specified, best attempt is made
     to use the available cores in the system for parallel generation. A
     value greater than 1 can be specified to indicate the level of
     parallelism to use. To disable parallel generation, set value to
     "off".

--parallel-executors-max-heap-size=<value>
     Optional. The maximum memory size to be used for allocations for
     parallel execution modules when running this tool with parallel
     mode enabled. This value is specified as <size><unit> where unit
     can be m (or M) for multiples of megabytes or g (or G) for
     multiples of gigabytes. The default value is 512m. This settings
     has no effect when the parallel mode is not enabled.

--bypass-quartus-project
     Optional. Override Quartus Project settings with values from the
     Platform Designer project if possible. For example, if the Platform
     Designer project defines its own IP search path, use it instead of
     the one defined in the Quartus Project settings. This will mainly
     affect the generation process.

--simulator[=<value>]
     Optional. Repeatable. The specified simulator type(s) determine
     which simulation scripts will be generated. The allowed simulator
     types are: MODELSIM, VCSMX, VCX, RIVERIA, XCELIUM. The argument can
     be a single simulator type or a comma separated list of simulator
     types. For example: --simulator=MODELSIM or
     --simulator=VCS,RIVIERA,XCELIUM.
     If omitted, simulation scripts are generated for all types.

--system-verilog-wrapper
     Optional. If set, then create SystemVerilog top-level wrapper.

--jvm-max-heap-size=<value>
     Optional. The maximum memory size to be used for allocations when
     running this tool. This value is specified as <size><unit> where
     unit can be m (or M) for multiples of megabytes or g (or G) for
     multiples of gigabytes. The default value is 512m.

--help
     Optional. Display help for this tool

Usage: qsys-script

   OPTION                            DESCRIPTION
   --cmd=<value>                   ? Tcl commands string
   --script=<file>                 ? Tcl commands script file
   --package-version=<value>       ? Tcl commands package version
   --system-file=<file>            ? Platform Designer system file to load
   -sp, --search-path=<value>      ? Component search path 
   -qpf, --quartus-project=<value> ? Use Quartus Project
   --new-quartus-project=<value>   ? create a new Quartus Project
   -c, --rev=<value>               ? Quartus Project Revision
   --jvm-max-heap-size=<value>     ? Set the maximum heap memory size to be used
   -h, --help                      ? Show help

QSYS-SCRIPT
-----------
The qsys-script pro tool can be used to create and manipulate Platform
Designer systems using Tcl scripting commands. If a system is specified,
it will be loaded before any scripting commands are executed.

--cmd=<value>
     Optional. A string containing Tcl scripting commands for creating
     or manipulating Platform Designer systems. If a Tcl script file is
     also specified, commands in the script string will be run before
     the the contents of the script file.

--script=<file>
     Optional. A file containing Tcl scripting commands for creating or
     manipulating Platform Designer systems. If a Tcl command string is
     also specified, commands in the command string will be run before
     the commands in the script file are run.

--package-version=<value>
     Optional. Specify which version of the system scripting Tcl API to
     use. This version determines the availability and behavior of the
     Tcl commands. The minimum supported version is 12.0. If not
     specified, the Tcl script must request the system scripting API
     directly using the "package require -exact qsys <version>" command
     in the script.

--system-file=<file>
     Optional. Specifies the path to a .qsys system file. This system
     will be loaded before running any scripting commands.

--search-path=<value>
     Optional. If omitted, a standard default path will be used. If
     provided, a comma-separated list of paths will be searched. To
     include the standard path in your replacement, use "$", like
     "/extra/dir,$".

--quartus-project=<value>
     Optional. The name of the Quartus project file. You may provide the
     revision name using --rev; otherwise, the default revision
     associated with the Quartus project is used.

--new-quartus-project=<value>
     Optional. Create a new Quartus project with the specified path and
     name. You may provide the revision name using --rev; otherwise, the
     default revision name is the project name.

--rev=<value>
     Optional. The name of the Quartus project revision. This switch is
     ignored if it is provided without one of the quartus project
     switches.

--jvm-max-heap-size=<value>
     Optional. The maximum memory size to be used for allocations when
     running this tool. This value is specified as <size><unit> where
     unit can be m (or M) for multiples of megabytes or g (or G) for
     multiples of gigabytes. The default value is 512m.

--help
     Optional. Display help for this tool
